conflict_resolutions.NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW: The four current-law leads (33 CFR 148.737, 28 CFR part 61 Appendix E, 42 U.S.C. 4321 note and its Table IV listing) name EO 13148: the two regulations cite it in lists of authorities or policies, and the Code note prints EO 12088 as amended by EO 13148 section 901 and records EO 13148 as revoked by EO 13423 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t42-s4321.txt). A citation in current law does not keep a revoked order's commands in force, and EO 13423 section 11(a)(iv) revoked it in 2007 without savings, so the provisional status no stands.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 13148 of April 21, 2000, Greening the Government Through Leadership in Environmental Management (65 FR 24595); the number, date and title agree with the census register row. The text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, read in full. Inventory: the dossier inventory was corrected to the 94 scopes listed in the clause sheet: the issuing paragraph is added, heading-only fragments (secs. 305, 403, 404, 405, 406, 601, 701, 704, 902) are merged into their first subsection, sentences cut mid-way in secs. 501(b), 501(d), 501(e) and 503(b) are rejoined, the duplicate-suffixed scope of 501(d) is renamed, and page furniture and part headings are cut from span ends. Ending: the order has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause. The dossier's undated fixed-term features (the 12-month clock in section 702 and the exemption wording in section 801) are conditional action clocks and exemption wording, not ends, and the December 31, 2006 goals in sections 204, 205 and 503(a) are performance targets that were not ended by lapse. Executive Order 13423 section 11(a)(iv) revokes it by number, whole and without qualifier, so every clause except section 901 first ended on 2007-01-24; section 901 revoked other instruments on signing, 2000-04-21. Limitation: the Interagency Environmental Leadership Workgroup (section 306) and other bodies formed under the order may have had charters of their own that no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands. AI producer hypothesis; not certification.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined: (1) own terms: none, and every timed provision is a deadline, not an end; (2) amendment or supersession: a by-number search of held order texts finds the order cited only in EO 13327 and EO 13693 (EO 13693 section 16(d) amends EO 13327 and not this order), in EO 13423 (the revocation), and in the note to 42 U.S.C. 4321; none amends, extends or ends it before 2007-01-24; (3) the Federal Register disposition-note search lists EO 13423 as the only ending event; (4) EO 13423 is therefore the first instrument that revokes it. EO 13693 section 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 without reviving this order.","independent_command_check":"The order's commands are directed to executive agencies and officers; no independent statute or rule is shown to carry any of them forward. Statutory duties the order mentions (for example under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act or the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act) rest on those statutes and not on the order.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects are recorded in the savings reason: the revocations the order performed survive, and EO 13423 carries the subject forward as a successor.","scope_check":"The clause sheet covers every scope of the order from the issuing paragraph to the last section, and each scope ends on the same instrument except section 901, which was performed on signing. Amendments to the order by later instruments: none found."}

savings.reason: Executive Order 13423 section 11(a) revokes EOs 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number, with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sections 10(a) to (c) of EO 13423 are its own implementation and no-rights provisions. One effect of EO 13148 survives it: section 901 revoked EO 12843, EO 12856, the 1994 landscaping memorandum, EO 12969 and the pollution control plan section of EO 12088 on signing, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive what it revoked (accrued); the note to 42 U.S.C. 4321 still prints EO 12088 as amended by EO 13148 section 901. EO 13423 restates the environmental-management subject as duties of its own (sections 2(e), 3(b), 3(c) and 3(g)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order. EO 13693 section 16(d) amends EO 13327 section 3(b)(vi) by striking the citation of EO 13148 and amends nothing in EO 13148; EO 13693 section 16(a) revokes EO 13423 with no wording reviving EO 13148. The order created no fund, property or private right (section 902(a)). The held leads (33 CFR 148.737, 28 CFR part 61 Appendix E, 42 U.S.C. 4321 note) cite the order and none continues its commands; the Code note itself records EO 13148 as revoked by EO 13423.
